A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ResGen work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation and speech-synthesis results in Tables 1–3, plus sampling ablations in Appendix B.2.

after.justification: v3 reports original image and speech results, architectural ablations, reconstruction measurements, faster-MAR comparisons and masking-schedule experiments.

M1.justification: The core ResGen algorithm remains, but v3 adds substantial architectural variants. Rvqvae-ResGen uses a separately trained waveform/STFT autoencoder with ConvNeXt blocks and 72 RVQ levels alongside the existing 32-level MelVAE approach. AR-ResGen retains autoregressive spatial generation while replacing RQ-Transformer's depth transformer with a cumulative-embedding MLP; a direct-token prediction variant is also introduced.

E1.justification: The explicit evaluations remain ImageNet 256×256 and speech continuation/cross-sentence generation. However, v3 newly acknowledges using AI-Hub datasets, while v1 does not identify the speech corpora. The PDFs do not establish whether this represents additional data coverage or newly disclosed provenance.

E2.justification: The same-RVQ comparison expands from RQ-Transformer alone in v1 to include a depth-wise MaskGIT adaptation in v3 Table 1. Table 8 adds MAGVIT-v2 and MaskBit comparisons using their published scores. These materially broaden the relevant masked-generation comparisons; the external speech comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The depth-4 vision comparison is replaced by depth-16 comparisons with near-matched model sizes and a shared 2.8M-step training budget. Speech evaluation changes from 16 to 25 inference steps and includes 32- and 72-level codecs. New experiments vary MAR autoregressive/diffusion steps and cross-evaluate masking schedules using models trained for 400K iterations with EMA checkpoints.

E4.justification: The original sampling-step, top-p and temperature study is retained. v3 adds direct-token versus cumulative-embedding prediction, AR-ResGen controls isolating depth prediction, parameter scaling, reconstruction/generation quality versus RVQ depth, faster-MAR sweeps and training/sampling schedule sensitivity (Table 1, Figure 3 and Tables 5–7). These substantially expand the questions tested.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The additional experiments retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: The main depth-16 guided image FID changes from 1.95 to 1.93. Table 3 replaces the original speech model's continuation/cross-sentence WER of 1.79/1.72 with Melvae-ResGen results of 1.94/1.75 and Rvqvae-ResGen results of 1.86/1.70. These speech results use changed models and inference settings, so they are not same-setting gains or losses. v3 also adds substantial architectural, reconstruction, MAR and masking-schedule results.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds explicit asymptotic projection-cost estimates, including O(O*K*H) and the low-rank expression O(O*K*h + H*h). The existing discrete-diffusion formulation, variational bounds and Jensen-based objective derivation remain substantively unchanged; their notation and equation-number changes are presentational.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central contributions: cumulative RVQ-embedding prediction, masking within a diffusion/variational framework, and efficient high-fidelity image and speech generation with inference steps decoupled from RVQ depth. The new experiments principally support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations of depth-specific efficiency gains, MAR latency versus throughput, masking-schedule behavior, and architectural tradeoffs against VAR and LFQ-based models. It acknowledges MAGVIT-v2 and MaskBit's lower FID while arguing for representation flexibility. The original KV-caching, FSQ and missing low-step theoretical justification limitations are relocated unchanged to Appendix D.

D1.justification: v3 specifies the training masking function, codebook size, projection dimensions and detailed waveform-autoencoder architecture and losses. Table 4 supplies exact guidance schedules, top-p and temperatures. It also first specifies 50K samples for FID and A100 timing hardware, adds AI-Hub attribution and changes the project-page address. These substantially improve documentation without establishing that every newly disclosed setting changed.

R1.justification: Section 4 adds substantive positioning against HART, MAGVIT-v2 and MaskBit while removing the opening VQ-GAN/DALL-E discussion. Appendix C develops extensive distinctions from VAR, MAR and LFQ-based masked models. ConvNeXt and Vocos references support the new audio architecture; publication updates to existing references are not counted as new works.

P1.justification: The abstract, related-work discussion and experimental narrative are substantially rewritten. Vision results are reorganized into ablation and benchmark subsections, training details are organized by modality, additional discussion forms Appendix C, and the former Section 7 becomes Appendix D. ResGen-d8/d16 terminology changes to ResGen-rvq8/rvq16.

P2.justification: The small original Table 2 is replaced by a two-part ablation table. v3 adds Tables 4–8 and the RVQ-depth reconstruction/generation plot, and expands the speech table. Figure 1's arrows and labels and Figure 2's curves/captions are revised. The original sampling plot and image galleries are retained with renumbering.

improvement.justification: v1's single same-token vision comparison did not isolate depth prediction from the generation framework. v3's controlled Table 1 comparisons and AR-ResGen directly address this weakness, while the additional sensitivity studies, faster-MAR comparisons and detailed settings substantially improve experimental rigor and reproducibility. Some new interpretations overgeneralize: Table 7's exponential-sampling advantage depends on classifier-free guidance. These limitations do not outweigh the substantial improvement in evidence and transparency.
